_comment: Reviewed exemptions for scripts/quality/check-query-predicate-compilable.py. Each entry means: a
human looked at this declared `where`, confirmed it does NOT compile under the grammar the runtime
now enforces (LC-P0), and filed the finding -- so the detector measures NEW breakage instead of
re-reporting a known one. The key is '<corpus label>::<location>', so renaming the model or moving
the query invalidates the exemption and it resurfaces for re-review -- which is the point.
An entry REQUIRES a REG-nn/B-nn citation. An exempted predicate is still broken at runtime: it is
refused by name, not silently applied. Exempting it here suppresses the GATE, never the error.

AppGen/apps/pack-sample::queries[SalesBy.why: REG-101 -- declares queries[].parameters and a ':storeId' bind placeholder that NOTHING substitutes. Under the old engine this compared every Sale.storeId against the literal seven-character string ':storeId', so the query has returned zero rows for its whole life with no error anywhere; under LC-P0 it is refused by name. Widening the grammar to ACCEPT ':storeId' without substituting it would restore exactly the silent wrong answer LC-P0 exists to remove, so the shape stays refused until parameter substitution is implemented (REG-101 fix shape (a)-(c)).
